rules.title: Driver Privacy Act (SB 6002)
rules.statutory_language: "on or immediately surrounding" the protected premises (no numeric distance given)
rules.statutory_exclusions: SB 6002 excludes "automated school bus safety cameras, speed safety camera systems, and automated traffic safety camera systems, as defined in RCW 46.63.210" from its ALPR definition. A device of those types is not covered by this rule - verify device type before reporting.

guideline_rules.title: FDOT ALPR right-of-way permit revocation (EOM 26-01)
guideline_rules.summary: FDOT revoked all ALPR general-use permits on the State Highway System, ordered removal by 2026-09-30, and denies new requests. Applies to state highway right-of-way only; city, county, and private placements are unaffected. A camera still mapped on a state road is either stale map data or still installed.

guideline_rules.title: TxDOT pause on ALPR permits for state roads
guideline_rules.summary: At the Governor's direction TxDOT stopped issuing ALPR permits for state-owned roadways, including approved-but-not-installed ones. Existing cameras are not required to come down. Cameras first mapped after the pause date may be new installs, or older cameras mapped late, so they are only "possibly" a problem. Not a statute.

guideline_rules.title: CT Public Act 26-14 sec. 13(d): fixed readers near protected facilities
guideline_rules.summary: Bars collecting data from fixed readers on the premises of, or within a distance the POST Council will set of, a reproductive or sexual health facility that primarily provides gender-affirming care, if the facility notified the Council of its location. Distance not set yet, the registry is opt-in, and the map cannot tell which clinics provide gender-affirming care, so these are candidates only.

guideline_rules.title: CT Public Act 26-14 sec. 13(d): fixed readers near protected facilities
guideline_rules.summary: Same provision, for nonprofits primarily serving immigrant communities that notified the POST Council of their location. Distance not set yet, registry is opt-in, and the map cannot see the registry or tell nonprofits from other immigration services, so these are candidates only.

states_reviewed.summary: SB 274 (2025) sensitive-location placement language vetoed; not law.
2026 retention law only; no siting restriction.
RSA 261:75-b restricts use/retention, not placement near protected sites.
29-A M.R.S. §2117-A use/retention limits; no siting language.
Transparency/use rules only; no protected-location siting ban.

No enacted statutory law. Alabama Criminal Justice Information Center issued administrative rules (Ala. Admin. Code r. 265-X-6-.01 et seq., eff. March 17, 2022) covering law enforcement ALPR use, retention, registry, and audits. Agency regulation, not a statute. No siting restrictions.
No ALPR-specific statute found; confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey and obscureiq.com 2026 map. General surveillance and privacy laws apply by default.
No ALPR-specific statute. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey. Local agency policies govern use.

Has ALPR statute: Ark. Code Ann. §§ 12-12-1801 to 12-12-1808 ('Automatic License Plate Reader System Act'), originally enacted Act 1491 (2013), significantly amended by Act 668 / SB 446 (signed April 2025, 95th General Assembly). The amendment allows private landowners and businesses to use ALPRs (data deleted after 60 days; state agencies and parking enforcement up to 150 days). Permissible users and retention only; no siting restrictions.

No ALPR-specific statute. C.R.S. § 24-72-113 (enacted 2010, still current) limits retention of all government 'passive surveillance records' - a category that CDOT guidance explicitly includes ALPR imagery - to 3 years, with access restrictions after year 1.

Has ALPR statute: Connecticut Public Act 26-14 (SB 397), sec. 13, signed 2026-05-04, operating limits effective October 1, 2026: purpose limits, 21-day retention, and data-sharing tiers. No general siting restrictions; see the spirit-of rules for the one placement-related provision.
No ALPR-specific statute. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey and obscureiq 2026. Agency-level policies govern use.

No enacted ALPR statute. DC Code §§ 50-2209.01-50-2209.11 covers automated traffic enforcement (speed/red-light cameras) but not ALPR surveillance. MPD operates on an internal policy of 30-day on-board / 90-day central-server retention.

Has ALPR statute: Fla. Stat. § 316.0777. Covers FDOT right-of-way installation at law enforcement request (agency pays, removable on 30 days notice), bars use for traffic citations, and makes data confidential. No siting restrictions near protected locations. FDOT separately revoked state-highway ALPR permits in 2026 (executive action; see the spirit-of rules).

No ALPR-specific statute in O.C.G.A. Georgia DOT issues administrative permits for ALPR placement on state right-of-way (operational/infrastructure permits), but no privacy or data-focused ALPR statute exists.
No ALPR-specific statute. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey. No siting restrictions.

Has ALPR statute: Idaho Code § 49-1432 (enacted by S1180, Ch. 316, signed April 4, 2025, effective July 1, 2025). Limits agency use to criminal and traffic-accident investigations, missing persons, and traffic flow; requires access controls, training, and audits. No siting restrictions.

Has ALPR statute: 625 ILCS 5/2-130, enacted by Public Act 103-540 (eff. January 1, 2024). Bars sharing ALPR data with out-of-state agencies without written certification it won't be used for immigration or reproductive health care enforcement; data is confidential. No siting restrictions.
No ALPR-specific statute. Rapid Flock Safety deployment in Indianapolis, Fishers, Muncie, Gary with no state statutory framework. Agency policies govern.
No ALPR-specific statute. ACLU Iowa documented widespread LE deployment with no binding state-level statute as of 2025. Agency policies govern.

No ALPR statute. SB 305 (2021) would have regulated collection, use, and storage of ALPR data but did not become law. Kansas Legislative Research Dept documented abuse cases. Agency policies and MOUs govern retention (typically 6 months). No siting restrictions.

HB 58 (2026) enacted, effective 2026-07-15: permitted uses, 90-day retention, disclosure limits, penalties. Installation on highway rights-of-way needs a Transportation Cabinet permit (a permitting rule, not a protected-location restriction).
No ALPR-specific statute. Agency-level policies govern. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey. No siting restrictions.

Has ALPR statute: Md. Code, Public Safety § 3-509, as amended by HB 1081 / SB 840 (enacted 2024, effective October 1, 2024). Prohibits LE agencies and their contracted vendors from selling ALPR data or licensing/subscribing access to it, limits vendor access and outside uploads (MCAC only), and mandates audits and breach notification. No siting restrictions.

No enacted ALPR statute. H.3755 (194th General Court, 2025-26), 'An Act Establishing Driver Privacy Protections,' was favorably reported by committee and referred to House Ways & Means as of March 23, 2026; not enacted as of July 2026.
No ALPR-specific statute. Significant Flock deployment in metro Detroit, Grand Rapids, and Lansing with no statutory protections as of 2025. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey and unflocked.org.

Has ALPR statute: Minn. Stat. § 13.824 (enacted 2015, amended; Data Practices Act chapter) + § 626.8472 (policy requirement). Data is private, destroyed within 60 days unless tied to an investigation, tracking needs a warrant, with public logs and biennial audits. No siting restrictions.
No ALPR-specific statute. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey and obscureiq 2026. Agency policies govern.
No ALPR-specific statute. HB 658 (2025) introduced but did not advance. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 and stateline.org Oct 2025.

Has ALPR statute: Mont. Code Ann. § 46-5-117 (enacted via SB 344, signed May 8, 2023; 'Revise license plate laws'). Near-prohibition on government ALPR use on public highways, with exceptions (DOT planning, parking, truck screening, and law enforcement with a posted policy, annual audits, and listed purposes). Not a warrant requirement. No siting restrictions near schools, worship, or healthcare.
Has ALPR statute: Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 60-3201 to 60-3209 ('Automatic License Plate Reader Privacy Act,' enacted 2018). Limits retention to 180 days unless flagged as evidence in a criminal proceeding.
No ALPR-specific statute. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey. Agency policies govern.

Has ALPR statute: New Jersey Privacy Protection Act (A4070 / S4070), enacted and signed March 25, 2026. Limits selling or sharing ALPR data (law enforcement for lawful purposes only), bars sharing for civil immigration enforcement, and exempts data from OPRA. No siting restrictions.

SB 40 "Driver Privacy and Safety Act" (2026), effective 2026-07-01. Limits sharing (immigration, protected health care, protected speech), makes data confidential, requires annual reporting. No placement restrictions.
No enacted ALPR statute. Bills requiring minimum ALPR policy standards and mandatory posting (A4157/S3165 in 2023-24; S963/A907 in 2025-26) have passed the Assembly repeatedly but died in the Senate.
No ALPR-specific statute. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey and obscureiq 2026.
No ALPR-specific statute. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey and obscureiq 2026. General surveillance laws apply.
No enacted ALPR statute. SB 857 (2025) introduced but did not advance (confirmed by Stateline Oct 2025). No siting restrictions in the failed bill.

No enacted ALPR statute. SB 933 (2025-26 session, sponsors Picozzi et al.) would provide for ALPR systems under Title 75 (Vehicles); referred to Transportation Committee July 14, 2025; status pending as of research date.
No enacted ALPR statute. H5659 (2025 session) introduced but did not advance (confirmed by Stateline Oct 2025). No siting restrictions in the failed bill.

No enacted ALPR statute. H.3374 (2023-24) and H.4013 (2025-26) introduced provisions on permitted entities, DOT permit for non- interstate ROW placement, and retention - but neither has been enacted. H.4013 remains pending in 2025-26 session.
No ALPR-specific statute. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey and obscureiq 2026.

Has ALPR statute: Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-10-302 (enacted by 2014 Acts ch. 625, effective July 1, 2014). Caps storage of captured plate data from fixed cameras at 90 days unless part of an ongoing criminal investigation. No siting restrictions.

No ALPR-specific statute. HB 2083 (2025) died in committee without a vote. TxDOT paused new ALPR permits on state roads in September 2026 at the Governor's direction (executive action; see the spirit-of rules).

Has ALPR statute: Utah Code Ann. §§ 41-6a-2001 to 41-6a-2006 ('Automatic License Plate Reader System Act,' enacted 2013, amended by Ch. 251, 2024 General Session). Limits use to law enforcement business, retention to 9 months, with audits and annual reports. Stationary ALPRs on state highways need a UDOT permit (right-of-way permitting, not a protected- location rule). No siting restrictions near schools, worship, or healthcare.

Has ALPR statute: 23 V.S.A. § 1607 (enacted 2013 No. 69, most recently amended by 2023 No. 135 (Adj. Sess.) § 1a, effective July 1, 2025). Requires operator certification, limits data access to law enforcement (older data needs written justification or a warrant), and caps retention at 18 months. Repeal and state-agency use ban scheduled 2027-07-01 (use ban, not siting). No siting restrictions.
No ALPR-specific statute. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey and obscureiq 2026.
No enacted ALPR statute. ACLU Wisconsin documented multiple abuse cases in 2025; legislative proposals introduced but not passed as of 2026. Confirmed by unflocked.org and LAPPA survey.
No ALPR-specific statute. Confirmed by LAPPA Sept 2025 survey and obscureiq 2026.
